vi scrivo dal villaggio di cui vi avevo.easy: I am writing to you from the village I told you about. I arrived on the evening train, with an umbrella that did not help at all. The parish priest, a kind and very tired man, gave me the keys to the old sacristy. Behind a wooden wardrobe there was a door closed up with bricks. Behind the door there were six crates full of documents.
vi scrivo dal villaggio di cui vi avevo.short: I write from the village I told you of. The priest gave me the keys to the old sacristy: behind a bricked-up door were six crates of documents.

Verbali di seduta, lettere mai spedite,.easy: There are séance records, letters that were never sent, torn diary pages, articles from the local newspaper and old telegrams. They tell the story of fifty years and three generations of the same family: scientists, or so they called themselves, who for half a century tried to talk to the dead. And it seems that sometimes someone answered.
Verbali di seduta, lettere mai spedite,.short: Minutes, letters, diaries and telegrams: fifty years of a family of scientists who tried to speak with the dead. And sometimes, it seems, were answered.

Ho deciso di ordinarli e di trascriverli.easy: I decided to put the documents in order and copy them before I judge anything. The first document is about a wake. I ask you to read it the way I did: with the doubt the Society asks for, and with the window closed.
Ho deciso di ordinarli e di trascriverli.short: I have sorted and copied them. The first is the record of a wake: read it with scepticism, and with the window shut.

Da qualche giorno, quando attraversi {0}.easy: For some days now, when you walk through {0}, people make the sign of the cross. Children stop playing and dogs lower their tails. At night, under your window, there are bare footprints: they go up to the wall and do not come back. Something has decided that you are the most interesting person in town.
Da qualche giorno, quando attraversi {0}.short: In {0} people cross themselves as you pass. Under your window, bare footprints lead to the wall and never come back. Something has chosen you.

Una mattina, sulla soglia, trovi un rega.easy: One morning you find a gift in front of your door. It is better not to ask where it comes from.

All'inizio è solo un brusio, come una st.easy: At first you hear only a murmur, like many people in a room of the house next door. Then you understand the words. Then you hear the voices: an old woman looking for a ring, a child who counts to a hundred and starts again, a man who always repeats the same address. None of them seems to know they are dead.
All'inizio è solo un brusio, come una st.short: First a murmur, then voices: an old woman seeking a ring, a child counting, a man repeating an address. None of them knows they are dead.

Una mattina apri il Journal e trovi una.easy: One morning you open the Journal and find a page you did not write. The handwriting leans backwards and the ink is still wet. The formula on the page has only one mistake, as if the writer wanted to see if you would notice.
Una mattina apri il Journal e trovi una.short: In the Journal is a page you did not write, the ink still wet, with a single mistake, like a test.

Te ne accorgi. Sotto la correzione, qual.easy: You notice. Under your correction, someone has written one word: *"Good."*

Il tuo nome gira per {0}: al mercato, in.easy: In {0} everyone talks about you: at the market, in church, in the taverns. Some are afraid, others admire you, but they all speak quietly. A few days later you receive a card with a black border: it invites you "to a dinner among people who will not resign themselves". Inside the envelope, as a kindness, there is money.
Il tuo nome gira per {0}: al mercato, in.short: All {0} is talking about you, quietly. A black-edged card invites you "to a dinner among people who will not resign themselves", with money inside.

Il padre fu sepolto il giorno dei morti,.easy: Father was buried on the Day of the Dead, under a light rain. Many people from the village came to the cemetery, but they stayed behind the low wall: no one wanted to go near the grave, and the gravedigger worked fast without looking in. People said that in his last years the old man had stayed shut up in the estate, with machines that made noise at night. Sometimes, from the windows of his laboratory, came a light of a strange colour that no one could describe.
Il padre fu sepolto il giorno dei morti,.short: Father was buried on the Day of the Dead. The village kept behind the cemetery wall: people said the old man had worked at night on humming machines, amid lights of a nameless colour.

Gli eredi erano arrivati con la diligenz.easy: The heirs had arrived the evening before by coach. Each came from a different city, with a trunk and the same letter from the notary. Now the estate was theirs, and so were the debts, the instruments, the animals in the cages and Father's Journal: a leather notebook full of notes, drawings and formulae. On the last page there was only one sentence, underlined twice, so hard that the pen had cut the paper:
Gli eredi erano arrivati con la diligenz.short: The heirs inherited the estate, the debts, the laboratory and Father's Journal. On its last page, one sentence, underlined so hard it cut the paper:

Padre Anzelm benedisse la salma, chiuse.easy: Father Anzelm blessed the body and closed his prayer book. Then he told the heirs, loudly enough for everyone to hear, that he would pray very hard for their souls.
Padre Anzelm benedisse la salma, chiuse.short: Father Anzelm blessed the body and promised, loudly, to pray hard for the heirs' souls.

Non riesco a dormire. La camera che mi h.easy: I cannot sleep. They gave me our father's room: the bed still has the shape of his body and the air smells of camphor and acid. I put out the candle an hour ago, and then I hear the first knock.
Non riesco a dormire. La camera che mi h.short: I lie awake in our father's room. Then I hear the first knock.

Viene dalla parete dietro la testiera. U.easy: The sound comes from the wall behind the bed. A sharp knock, like a knuckle on wood. Then two knocks. Then one. Then nothing, for so long that I almost think I dreamt it. Then they start again, always the same and patient, like someone knocking at a door who knows someone is home.
Viene dalla parete dietro la testiera. U.short: Knocks on the wall behind the bed: one, two, one. Then silence, and again, patient, like someone who knows you are home.

Nella sua biblioteca ho visto un librett.easy: In his library I saw a little French book about talking tables: one knock means yes, two mean no. I remember it now, in the dark, and I wish I did not.
Nella sua biblioteca ho visto un librett.short: I remember a little book from his library: one knock for yes, two for no. I wish I did not.

Chiedo, a voce bassissima, se è lui. Un.easy: I ask, very quietly, if it is him. One knock. I ask if he is at peace. Two knocks, so strong that the jug shakes on the chest of drawers. Then silence, and a smell of wax, even though no candle is lit in the room. In the morning my fingers are numb and the Journal is open on the pillow, at a page I do not remember ever reading.
Chiedo, a voce bassissima, se è lui. Un.short: Is it him? One knock. Is he at peace? Two knocks, very hard. In the morning the Journal lies open on my pillow, at a page I never read.

Sveglio il servitore e lo mando in paese.easy: I wake the servant and send him to the village with the lantern. Father Anzelm arrives an hour later, with his stole over his nightshirt and holy water in a chemist's bottle. He blesses the wall, the bed, the window and, to be safe, me too.
Sveglio il servitore e lo mando in paese.short: I send for Father Anzelm. He comes in his nightshirt and blesses the wall, the bed and, to be thorough, me.

I colpi tacciono subito. Il prete, però,.easy: The knocking stops at once. But the priest stays at the door longer than he needs to and looks around: the cages, the glass instruments, the Journal open on the table. Before he leaves he shakes my hand and gives me a few coins "for the household, until everything is in order". It feels more like an advance than help.
I colpi tacciono subito. Il prete, però,.short: The knocking stops. The priest looks around a long time, then leaves me a few coins "for the household". It feels like a down payment.

Mi infilo sotto le coperte e premo il cu.easy: I get under the covers and press the pillow on my ears, as we did as children during storms. The knocking goes on for a long time, more softly. At some point it seems to move: from the wall to the floor, from the floor to the bed, very close to my ear. Then, at last, it ends.
Mi infilo sotto le coperte e premo il cu.short: Under the covers, pillow over my ears, I hear the knocking creep closer, right up to my ear. Then at last it stops.

All'alba scosto la tenda. Sulla parete,.easy: At dawn I open the curtain. On the wall, at the height of my head, the plaster is worn away in a small, regular circle, as if a knuckle had knocked there for years.
All'alba scosto la tenda. Sulla parete,.short: At dawn there is a small worn circle on the wall, as if a knuckle had knocked there for years.

A colazione nessuno parla dei colpi. Il.easy: At breakfast no one talks about the knocking. The coffee is too strong, the bread is old and everyone looks tired. Someone makes a joke about the mice in the attic, but no one laughs.
A colazione nessuno parla dei colpi. Il.short: At breakfast no one mentions the knocking, and no one laughs at the jokes about mice.

Dalla finestra della sala da pranzo si v.easy: From the dining-room window you can see the village: a few wooden houses near the church, smoke from the chimneys, the market opening. It is a poor place where people do not trust strangers. But Father has left his heirs an estate, a laboratory and a name that still makes people speak quietly. And a name, if you know how to use it, is worth a lot of money.
Dalla finestra della sala da pranzo si v.short: The village is poor and suspicious. But Father left his heirs an estate, a laboratory and a name that still makes people lower their voices: capital, for those who know how to use it.

Una carovana si è fermata ai margini del.easy: A caravan has stopped near the village. People say that a woman travels in it who talks to the dead, and that the dead answer her.
Una carovana si è fermata ai margini del.short: The wagon of a woman who talks with the dead has come to the village.

Il carro di Madame Vámos è dipinto di bl.easy: Madame Vámos's wagon is painted dark blue and covered in worn gold stars. It has tall wheels, velvet curtains and, on the door, a picture of an open hand with an eye in the palm. It has been near the village for three weeks, and in that time half the widows of {0} have gone inside at least once, without telling the priest.
Il carro di Madame Vámos è dipinto di bl.short: Madame Vámos's wagon, midnight blue with a hand and an eye on the door, has stood there three weeks. Half the widows of {0} have secretly been inside.

Stamattina la medium si è presentata all.easy: This morning the medium came to the estate. She is a small woman, and it is hard to tell how old she is. She wears a black shawl, speaks softly with a strange accent, and has very white, very cold hands. She said she had heard the knocking. No one had told her about it: she had *heard* it herself, from the road, passing the gate on the night of the dead.
Stamattina la medium si è presentata all.short: The medium, small and ageless, came to the estate. She says she *heard* the knocking from the road, on the night of the dead.

\"Vostro padre ha qualcosa da dire\", ci.easy: "Your father has something to say," she told us. "And he does not like to speak to people who will not listen." Then she invited all of us to a séance in her wagon, tomorrow at midnight. She did not ask for money. That worries me more than anything.
\"Vostro padre ha qualcosa da dire\", ci.short: "Your father has something to say." She invited us to a séance tomorrow at midnight, free of charge. That is what worries me.

Nessuno va. Madame Vámos accende le cand.easy: No one goes. Madame Vámos lights the candles, sits at the little table and waits until dawn in front of empty chairs. The baker's boy walks past at four and swears he heard her talking to someone, and heard someone answer.
Nessuno va. Madame Vámos accende le cand.short: No one goes. Madame waits until dawn before empty chairs; the baker's boy swears he heard her talking, and someone answering.

Quella notte, alla tenuta, i colpi raddo.easy: That night, at the estate, there are twice as many knocks. They knock on every wall, every door, everyone's bed. They knock like someone who has been left outside in the cold.
Quella notte, alla tenuta, i colpi raddo.short: That night the knocking doubles, everywhere, like someone left out in the cold.

Tutti gli eredi siedono intorno al tavol.easy: All the heirs sit around the little round table, in the wagon that smells of incense and horse. Madame asks them to hold hands; her fingers are freezing. She says something in a language no one knows, then she is silent. In the silence the table creaks, tips and rises a hand's width off the floor, with all their hands on it.
Tutti gli eredi siedono intorno al tavol.short: The heirs join hands around the table. Madame recites unknown words, and the table rises a hand's breadth off the floor.

Resta sospeso per il tempo di un respiro.easy: It stays in the air for the time of one breath. Then it falls with a single sharp knock. Madame opens her eyes and smiles, like someone who has just had good news. "He recognised you," she says. "All of you."
Resta sospeso per il tempo di un respiro.short: The table drops with one knock. Madame smiles: "He recognised you. All of you."

Solo alcuni degli eredi salgono sul carr.easy: Only some of the heirs get into the wagon. The others stay at the estate, in front of the fire, and tell each other that someone in the family must have a little common sense.
Solo alcuni degli eredi salgono sul carr.short: Only some of the heirs go; the others stay home, out of common sense.

Verso l'una di notte, dalla direzione de.easy: Around one in the morning, a scream comes from the village. Then another. Then a laugh, but it is not clear whose. Those who come back at dawn do not want to say what they saw. But their hands are as cold as Madame's, and all morning they look at the walls.
Verso l'una di notte, dalla direzione de.short: In the night, screams and a laugh from the village. Those who return at dawn say nothing, their hands cold as Madame's, eyes on the walls.

**LA STREGA DEL CARRO.** Domenica scorsa.easy: **THE WITCH OF THE WAGON.** Last Sunday Father Anzelm spoke for the whole sermon about what he called, very clearly, "the witch of the wagon". He reminded the faithful that the dead rest with God, not inside a little table, and that whoever disturbs them for money also disturbs God. Then, looking at the pews at the back, he said that some families who had arrived recently should remember this.
**LA STREGA DEL CARRO.** Domenica scorsa.short: **THE WITCH OF THE WAGON.** Father Anzelm's sermon was about "the witch of the wagon": the dead rest with God, and certain newly arrived families would do well to remember it.

Il sermone è stato molto apprezzato. Lun.easy: People liked the sermon very much. On Monday, however, this newspaper saw many ladies dressed in black coming and going on the road to the estate. The widows of {0} have lost husbands, sons and brothers to the cold, fevers and hunger. They want news of their loved ones, and for loved ones, as everyone knows, people pay gladly.
Il sermone è stato molto apprezzato. Lun.short: On Monday, though, many widows of {0} take the road to the estate: they want news of their dead, and will pay for it.

Qualcuno nel villaggio scrive lettere, e.easy: Someone in the village writes letters without signing them. The envelopes come without stamps, and no one sees them arrive.

Negli anni della maturità la famiglia co.easy: In the middle years the family receives letters that the postman never brought. The letters appear under the door, in the bread basket, once even inside Father's Journal, locked in the desk. They are envelopes of heavy paper, with no address and no signature, closed with black wax. In the wax there is the picture of an open eye.
Negli anni della maturità la famiglia co.short: Letters arrive that no one delivered, even inside the locked Journal. No address, no signature: only an open eye in black wax.

Dentro, ogni volta, poche righe in una c.easy: Inside there are always a few lines, in elegant, old-fashioned handwriting. The **Circle of the Last Hour** greets the heirs of the great scientist, knows their work, admires their courage and wants to meet them, one at a time, in a private place. They only need to go to the address given and say the right word.
Dentro, ogni volta, poche righe in una c.short: The **Circle of the Last Hour** wishes to meet the heirs, one by one, in secret: go to the address given and say the right word.

Ti aspetta un uomo alto, in un cappotto.easy: A tall man is waiting for you, with a coat too elegant for {0} and a black carnation in his buttonhole. He does not ask who you are. He calls you by name, gives you his arm and walks with you, slowly, as old friends do.
Ti aspetta un uomo alto, in un cappotto.short: A tall man with a black carnation awaits you. He knows your name and walks with you like an old friend.

\"Il Circolo dell'Ultima Ora\", dice, \".easy: "The Circle of the Last Hour," he says, "is a small group of people who will not resign themselves. We have all lost someone, and we have all found out that the dead are not as far away as the priests say. Madame Vámos is our voice. Your father was… let us say a correspondent."
\"Il Circolo dell'Ultima Ora\", dice, \".short: "We are people who will not resign ourselves: the dead are not as far as the priests say. Madame Vámos is our voice. Your father was… a correspondent."

Ti porge una busta, gonfia di fogli. \"Q.easy: He gives you an envelope full of pages. "Here are things he knew and did not have time to teach you. They are yours. In return we want only a promise: that one day, when the Circle asks you, you will open the door."
Ti porge una busta, gonfia di fogli. \"Q.short: He hands you an envelope: "What your father knew. In return, a promise: when the Circle asks, you will open the door."

Stringi la mano dell'uomo. È fredda come.easy: You shake the man's hand. It is as cold as Madame's and it does not get warm in yours. "The Circle thanks you," he says, and leaves without turning round.
Stringi la mano dell'uomo. È fredda come.short: His hand is as cold as Madame's. "The Circle thanks you."

La busta pesa più di quanto dovrebbe. Qu.easy: The envelope is heavier than it should be. That evening you read it by the light of the lamp and see that some pages are written by your father. One of them has a date two weeks after his death.
La busta pesa più di quanto dovrebbe. Qu.short: The envelope holds pages in your father's hand. One is dated two weeks after his death.

Restituisci la busta senza aprirla. L'uo.easy: You give the envelope back without opening it. The man is not offended. In fact, he seems almost happy, like someone who has won a small bet with himself. "Saying no is also a way of paying attention," he says. "We will meet again." He gives you a few coins "for the trouble" and leaves.
Restituisci la busta senza aprirla. L'uo.short: You return the envelope unopened. The man seems almost pleased. "We shall meet again." He leaves you a few coins and goes.

Il giorno dopo, al Cemetery, sulla tomba.easy: The next day, at the Cemetery, there is a black carnation on your father's grave. The earth around the headstone has been moved, as if someone had put an ear to it to listen.
Il giorno dopo, al Cemetery, sulla tomba.short: The next day there is a black carnation on your father's grave, and the earth has been disturbed.

Il consiglio si riunisce nella sala sopr.easy: The council meets in the room above the inn, because rain comes into the town hall. There are Mayor Bódi, the notary, three landowners, the schoolmaster and, on a separate chair, Father Anzelm. He cannot vote but he can speak, and he speaks for an hour and a half.
Il consiglio si riunisce nella sala sopr.short: The council meets above the inn. Father Anzelm has no vote, but speaks for an hour and a half.

La questione all'ordine del giorno è una.easy: There is only one question to decide: can Mrs Eszter Vámos, whose job is "consoler", stay in {0}? In eight years her wagon has become a house with the shutters always closed. Every Thursday her parlour fills with people who go in crying and come out smiling. And the Circle of the Last Hour, which no one admits to joining, has bought two plots near the cemetery.
La questione all'ordine del giorno è una.short: The question: may the "consoler" Eszter Vámos stay in {0}? In eight years her parlour has filled with the grieving, and the Circle has bought land beside the cemetery.

Il parroco parla di eresia, di truffa, d.easy: The priest talks about heresy, cheating, and grief used to make money. The notary says she pays her taxes. The Mayor does not speak: he listens and counts. In the end they decide, as {0} always does with difficult questions, to let the most important families of the village vote too. And by now the most important is the heirs' family.
Il parroco parla di eresia, di truffa, d.short: The priest cries heresy, the notary recalls taxes paid. In the end, as is the custom in {0}, the important families vote too. And the most important is the heirs'.

Madame Vámos resta. La sera stessa le fi.easy: Madame Vámos stays. That same evening the windows of her house light up one after another, and from the parlour comes the sound of a piano that no one in {0} ever saw arrive. The next week the Circle of the Last Hour rents a house on the square, right in front of the church, and puts up a brass sign with an open eye. Father Anzelm has the funeral bells rung for an hour, even though no one has died.
Madame Vámos resta. La sera stessa le fi.short: Madame Vámos stays, and the Circle opens premises on the square, opposite the church, with a brass eye on the door. Father Anzelm has the death knell rung.

Il carro, rimesso in ordine per l'occasi.easy: The wagon, tidied up for the occasion, leaves the village at dawn. Madame Vámos sits at the front, straight, and never turns round. Only when she passes the estate gate does she raise a white hand, as if waving to someone at the window. But there was no one at the window.
Il carro, rimesso in ordine per l'occasi.short: At dawn the wagon leaves. Passing the estate, Madame waves to someone at the window. There was no one at the window.

La mattina dopo, sulla porta della tenut.easy: The next morning someone has drawn an open eye in charcoal on the estate door. The servant washes it three times. After the third time the eye is still there, only a little lighter, as if it were looking up from under water.
La mattina dopo, sulla porta della tenut.short: A charcoal eye appears on the estate door. The servant washes it three times, but it stays.

I documenti della prima generazione si i.easy: The papers of the first generation end here. The parish records say that the family's scientists died in the following years, one at a time, of different illnesses and at different ages. They were buried in the cemetery of {0}, near their father. The priest writes, rather pleased, that the knocking on the estate's walls ended with the last funeral.
I documenti della prima generazione si i.short: The first generation's scientists died in the years that followed and were buried in {0}, beside their father. With the last funeral, the priest notes, the knocking stopped.

Annota anche, con meno soddisfazione, ch.easy: He also writes, less pleased, that none of those funerals could take place after sunset: when it got dark, the men would no longer lift the coffin. They said someone inside was knocking.
Annota anche, con meno soddisfazione, ch.short: But no funeral could be held after sunset: in the dark, the bearers heard knocking inside the coffin.

La seconda cassa si apre con un salto di.easy: The second crate jumps forward seventeen years. The papers of the first generation end in 1856. The others begin in the spring of 1873, when the heirs' children took over the estate, the laboratory and the Journal, which was now two and a half volumes long.
La seconda cassa si apre con un salto di.short: The second crate resumes in 1873: the heirs' children take the estate, the laboratory and the Journal, now two and a half volumes.

Il villaggio era cresciuto. Al posto del.easy: The village was bigger. Instead of wooden houses there were houses with painted beams, a stone street, a post office, two inns and a doctor. The priest was still Father Anzelm, older and thinner, but as stubborn as before. And there was, one of the new heirs writes to a sister, "this thing they call the veil here, as if it were the weather, like the rain or the fog".
Il villaggio era cresciuto. Al posto del.short: The village has grown; Father Anzelm is older but as stubborn as ever. And there is "this thing they call the veil here, like the rain or the fog".

Madame Vámos non era invecchiata: così,.easy: Madame Vámos had not grown older: at least, that is what everyone said. The Circle of the Last Hour no longer hid. It had premises on the square, a band for funerals and two hundred members, and that year it bought the land behind the town hall to build a temple.
Madame Vámos non era invecchiata: così,.short: Madame Vámos had not aged, and the Circle, now two hundred strong, bought land to build a temple.

Della donna del carro restavano solo le.easy: Of the woman in the wagon only the stories were left, and a strange habit: every now and then, on the doors of the houses of {0}, an eye drawn in charcoal appeared. No one said they had drawn it, and no one rubbed it out. People said the Circle of the Last Hour still met, but no one knew where, or who belonged to it.
Della donna del carro restavano solo le.short: Of the woman in the wagon only stories remained, and charcoal eyes on the doors of {0}. The Circle still met, no one knew where.

I colpi alle pareti erano cessati con l'.easy: The knocking on the walls had ended with the last funeral of the first generation. For seventeen years the estate had been a normal house: cold in winter, damp in summer, full of things no one had the courage to throw away.
I colpi alle pareti erano cessati con l'.short: For seventeen years the estate had been quiet, like any other house.

La prima notte che i nuovi eredi vi dorm.easy: The first night the new heirs sleep there, the knocking starts again. But this time, after the knocking, the voices come. They are voices each of them knows very well: they are the voices of their parents.
La prima notte che i nuovi eredi vi dorm.short: On the first night the knocking returns, and after it the voices: their parents' voices.

La voce arriva prima dei colpi: un bisbi.easy: The voice comes before the knocking. It is a fast whisper, with no pauses, that does not greet you or ask how you are. It talks about formulae, numbers, a mistake in the third notebook that must be fixed now, before it is too late. It is the voice of your father or your mother, and you know the tone too: the same as on the nights spent shut in the laboratory.
La voce arriva prima dei colpi: un bisbi.short: A whisper without pauses: formulae, numbers, a mistake to fix at once. It is your parent's voice, in the tone of nights in the laboratory.

\"Finisci tu\", ripete. \"Finisci tu, fi.easy: "You finish it," it says again and again. "You finish it, you finish it." At dawn your hand hurts and you have three full pages in handwriting that is not yours.
\"Finisci tu\", ripete. \"Finisci tu, fi.short: "You finish it." At dawn you have three pages in a hand not your own.

Non sono colpi: è un ticchettio rapido e.easy: It is not knocking: it is a fast, uneven tapping, like fingers beating on a table out of impatience. Then the voice comes, agitated, in the middle of a sentence started who knows when: "...and the numbers don't add up, they never add up, but you'll make them add up..."
Non sono colpi: è un ticchettio rapido e.short: An impatient tapping, then the voice: "...the numbers never add up, but you'll make them add up..."

Provi a chiedere se soffre. Non ti ascol.easy: You try to ask if they are suffering. They do not listen to you, just as they never did. When the tapping ends, you notice that you are tapping your fingers too, with the same rhythm, and you cannot stop.
Provi a chiedere se soffre. Non ti ascol.short: They do not listen, as always. Then you notice that you are drumming too, and cannot stop.

Il colpo è uno solo, lieve, come una man.easy: There is just one knock, soft, like a hand resting on the door. Then the voice, calm, almost amused: it asks if you eat enough, if the greenhouse roof still has holes, if you remember the miller's widow. "Tell her I'm well," it says.
Il colpo è uno solo, lieve, come una man.short: One gentle knock, then a calm voice asking if you eat enough. "Tell the miller's widow I'm well."

Capisci che non parla di sé. Parla di tu.easy: You understand that it is not talking about itself. It is talking about all the families it helped in life, who now, on the other side, stay close to it. Before leaving it blesses you, as it did when you went on a journey.
Capisci che non parla di sé. Parla di tu.short: The families it comforted in life now keep it company. Before leaving, it blesses you.

Nella stanza c'è profumo di pane caldo e.easy: The room smells of warm bread and lavender: the smell of the estate kitchen, many years ago. The voice does not knock. It speaks softly, as next to a sick person's bed, and tells you that it is not cold on the other side, and that the people it helped in life came to welcome it.
Nella stanza c'è profumo di pane caldo e.short: A smell of warm bread and lavender. A gentle voice tells you it is not cold on the other side, and that it is not alone.

\"Hai tempo\", dice. \"Usalo per i vivi..easy: "You have time," it says. "Use it for the living." In the morning, on the bedside table, there is something that was not there the evening before.
\"Hai tempo\", dice. \"Usalo per i vivi..short: "Use your time for the living." In the morning there is a gift on the bedside table.

La voce è bassa, guardinga, come chi par.easy: The voice is low and careful, like someone speaking in a room where another person is listening. "Listen carefully, because I won't be able to say this again. Many years ago I made a promise to the Circle, to a man with a black carnation. I thought I had sold something worth nothing. I was wrong."
La voce è bassa, guardinga, come chi par.short: A low, wary voice: "Long ago I made a promise to the Circle. I thought it was worth little. I was wrong."

Poi ti dice che cosa aveva promesso, par.easy: Then it tells you exactly what was promised, and who will have to open the door when the Circle knocks: you. "Tell no one," it says at the end. "But remember it. One day you will need to know how to break a promise."
Poi ti dice che cosa aveva promesso, par.short: It tells you the promise, word for word: you will be the one to open the door. "Remember it. One day you must know how to break it."

Prima della voce arriva l'odore: garofan.easy: Before the voice comes the smell: carnations and freshly dug earth. "The Circle is watching you," it whispers. "It watches all of us: those who signed and those born to those who signed."
Prima della voce arriva l'odore: garofan.short: A smell of carnations and earth. "The Circle is watching you: those who signed, and their children."

Ti racconta della busta, delle pagine sc.easy: It tells you about the envelope, the pages written by a dead hand and the promise to open a door. Then it tells you something the Circle does not know you know: the promise binds the whole family, but the family can choose not to keep it. There is a price, though. What it is, the voice cannot say: the knocking stops halfway.
Ti racconta della busta, delle pagine sc.short: The promise binds the blood, but the blood may choose not to keep it. At a price, which the broken-off knocking never names.

Un colpo, due, uno: lo stesso ritmo che.easy: One knock, two, one: the same rhythm you heard described a thousand times at the table, by the voice that is speaking to you now. "That night I answered first," it says. "The door opened a little for me, and it never closed again."
Un colpo, due, uno: lo stesso ritmo che.short: One, two, one. "That night I answered first. The door opened a little, and never closed again."

Poi, in fretta, come chi teme di essere.easy: Then, quickly, like someone afraid of being interrupted, it dictates the start of an experiment it never had the courage to try in life. You write until the candle is finished.
Poi, in fretta, come chi teme di essere.short: It hurriedly dictates an experiment it never dared try in life. You write until the candle dies.

La voce non perde tempo con i saluti. \".easy: The voice does not waste time on greetings. "You know how to answer, don't you? Once for yes, twice for no. I taught you, even if you don't remember: I tapped on your cradle, and you laughed."
La voce non perde tempo con i saluti. \".short: "You know how to answer, don't you? Once for yes, twice for no. I taught you, in your cradle."

Un brivido. \"Io risposi, la prima notte.easy: You shiver. "I answered, the first night, and since then everyone here can hear me. Now they can hear you too." When the voice stops, there is the drawing of an experiment on the table. And on the bedroom wall there are small knuckle marks, at the height of a cradle.
Un brivido. \"Io risposi, la prima notte.short: "Since I answered, everyone over here can hear me. Now they hear you too." The outline of an experiment is left on the table.

Colpi lontani, irregolari, come di qualc.easy: Distant, uneven knocking, like someone knocking at another house, in another street. You answer, but nothing happens. You call out, and the silence gets deeper.
Colpi lontani, irregolari, come di qualc.short: Distant knocking. You answer, you call: only silence.

Forse chi ti ha messo al mondo non vuole.easy: Maybe your father or your mother does not want to talk to you. Maybe they cannot. Or maybe, you think with a relief that makes you a little ashamed, they are just resting in peace.
Forse chi ti ha messo al mondo non vuole.short: Maybe they will not speak to you. Maybe they are simply at peace.

Aspetti fino all'alba con la candela acc.easy: You wait until dawn with the candle lit. You hear knocking on the walls of the other rooms, faraway voices, crying, a laugh. On your wall, nothing.
Aspetti fino all'alba con la candela acc.short: Until dawn you hear knocks and voices in the other rooms. On your wall, nothing.

Solo verso le cinque arriva un colpo leg.easy: Only around five does a very soft knock come, just one. Maybe it means yes. Or maybe it is only the wood moving in the cold.
Solo verso le cinque arriva un colpo leg.short: At five, one knock: perhaps a yes, perhaps the wood settling.

All'alba le voci tacciono. A colazione l.easy: At dawn the voices stop. At breakfast the family is strangely polite: they pass the butter, talk about the weather and no one looks anyone else in the eye.
All'alba le voci tacciono. A colazione l.short: At breakfast everyone is polite, and no one meets anyone's eye.

Ognuno ha sentito qualcosa. Nessuno sa c.easy: Each of them heard something. No one knows what the others heard. And all of them, at least for a moment, thought about telling a lie.

Nel secondo volume del Journal, tra una.easy: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe and a blacksmith's bill, there is the drawing of a machine for talking to the dead.

Paghi i muratori in contanti, davanti a.easy: You pay the builders in cash, in front of everyone. The Temple's foundations grow fast, too fast: the builders say that at night someone works in their place, and that in the morning they find the stones already cut.
Paghi i muratori in contanti, davanti a.short: You pay the masons. The Temple rises too fast: at night, they say, someone works in their place.

Madame Vámos passa a vedere il cantiere..easy: Madame Vámos comes to see the building site. She shakes your hand and calls you by name in front of everyone, as people do with family. That evening the widows of the Circle light a candle for your dead.
Madame Vámos passa a vedere il cantiere..short: Madame Vámos calls you by name in front of everyone, and the Circle's widows light a candle for your dead.

Il vecchio Padre Anzelm celebra una mess.easy: Old Father Anzelm says a mass for your family's dead, in the empty church, with only one altar boy, who yawns. At the end he takes your arm, with a strength you did not expect. "I buried them all, your family," he says. "Let them stay where I put them."
Il vecchio Padre Anzelm celebra una mess.short: After mass, old Father Anzelm grips your arm: "I buried them all, your people. Let them stay where I put them."

Quella notte, per la prima volta da mesi.easy: That night, for the first time in months, no one knocks in your room, and you sleep until it is full daylight.

Nel secondo volume del Journal, tra una.easy: In the second volume of the Journal, between a recipe for preserving tissue and a blacksmith's bill, I found the design. There are three drawings in ink, made with a care Grandfather gave to nothing else. He calls it the **Telegraph of the Dead**.
Nel secondo volume del Journal, tra una.short: In the Journal I found Grandfather's design, drawn with rare care: the **Telegraph of the Dead**.

Una batteria di vasi di vetro; chilometr.easy: There are glass jars connected together, miles of copper wire wound around a piece of iron, a keyboard of twenty-six bone keys. In the middle there is a needle inside a flask full of a gas he calls "veil air". According to his calculations the dead do not speak: they change the electric current, very slightly. A very sensitive needle is enough to read them.
Una batteria di vasi di vetro; chilometr.short: Glass jars, copper wire, a bone keyboard and a needle in a flask of "veil air". The dead, he believed, barely move the current: a sensitive needle can read them.

Ai margini della terza tavola c'è una no.easy: On the edge of the third drawing there is a note in pencil: *"I did not have the time. They will."* To build the first part we need many gears, many more than we have in the house. Each of us will have to decide how much work to take away from our own experiments.
Ai margini della terza tavola c'è una no.short: In the margin, in pencil: *"I did not have the time. They will."* It needs gears, and each of us must decide how many to spare.

Il primo stadio del Telegrafo occupa un'.easy: The first part of the Telegraph takes up a whole wall of the laboratory. On the night they switch it on, the glass jars hum, the lights in the whole house get dimmer and the needle, inside the flask, starts to shake.
Il primo stadio del Telegrafo occupa un'.short: The Telegraph fills a whole wall. When they switch it on, the lights dim and the needle begins to tremble.

Non è il tremito della corrente: è più l.easy: It is not shaking because of the current: it moves more slowly and more surely, like a finger looking for a letter on a keyboard. It stops on a bone key. Then on another. Before anyone can read the word, a fuse blows, and in the dark, for a moment, someone laughs.
Non è il tremito della corrente: è più l.short: The needle seeks letters, key by key. Before the word can be read a fuse blows, and in the dark someone laughs.

Gli ingranaggi raccolti bastano appena p.easy: The gears collected are only just enough for the base. The design goes back in the drawer, under the second volume of the Journal, and the pieces go back to the people who gave them.
Gli ingranaggi raccolti bastano appena p.short: There are not enough gears. The design goes back into the drawer.

Quella notte i colpi alle pareti sono pi.easy: That night the knocking on the walls is slower than usual, almost tired. If the dead can be disappointed, they are.

**LA NEBBIA NON SI ALZA.** Da undici gio.easy: **THE FOG WILL NOT LIFT.** For eleven days a thick white fog has covered {0} day and night. The doctor says it comes from the pond, the chemist says it comes from the estate, Father Anzelm says it is a punishment. Lanterns light only three steps ahead. Yesterday the coach arrived six hours late: the driver swears he went round and round the cemetery all night.
**LA NEBBIA NON SI ALZA.** Da undici gio.short: **THE FOG WILL NOT LIFT.** For eleven days fog has covered {0} day and night. The coach circled the cemetery all night.

Più strane ancora sono le testimonianze.easy: Even stranger are the stories that reach the newspaper. Mrs Tóth saw her husband, dead for nine years, waiting for her at the corner by the chemist's. The baker heard his mother calling him from the oven. Three children played all afternoon with a friend no adult saw, and whose name no one knows. We advise readers not to go out unless they must, and not to answer anyone who calls their name from the fog.
Più strane ancora sono le testimonianze.short: The dead are seen in the fog: a husband nine years buried, a mother calling from the oven, a nameless child. Do not answer anyone who calls you from the fog.

Nella nebbia il velo è sottile come cart.easy: In the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper. Someone wants to use it for their own good.

Nella saletta in fondo al Pub, dietro un.easy: In the small room at the back of the Pub, behind a velvet curtain, Madame Vámos sees anyone who buys the landlord a drink and asks no questions.
Nella saletta in fondo al Pub, dietro un.short: At the back of the Pub, Madame Vámos receives those who ask no questions.

Madame Vámos non c'è più, ma la sua sedi.easy: Madame Vámos is gone, but her chair is still in the small room at the back of the Pub. Whoever sits in front of it, with their hands on the little table, hears her voice.
Madame Vámos non c'è più, ma la sua sedi.short: Madame is gone, but whoever sits before her chair still hears her voice.

Nella saletta in fondo al Pub una ragazz.easy: In the small room at the back of the Pub a pale girl, who says she studied with the woman in the wagon, holds séances for a little money.
Nella saletta in fondo al Pub una ragazz.short: At the back of the Pub, a pupil of the woman in the wagon holds séances for a few coins.

La voce della medium si fa roca, maschil.easy: The medium's voice becomes rough, like a man's: it is a miller who died of cholera, she says, who trusted banks even less than priests. He describes a loose brick behind the stove of an abandoned mill. You go there the next day, with fog up to your knees. The brick is there. Behind it is a tin box full of coins, and no one, as far as you know, will ever come to take it.
La voce della medium si fa roca, maschil.short: A miller who died of cholera speaks and points you to a loose brick in an abandoned mill. Behind it is a box of coins no one will claim.

Le mani della medium stringono le tue, a.easy: The medium holds your hands for a long time. Then she says a name: that of the person in town who is most afraid of you and says bad things about you. You know that name. The next day you visit them with a basket of fruit and a smile. The rumours, strangely, stop.
Le mani della medium stringono le tue, a.short: The medium names the one spreading rumours about you. A visit with a basket of fruit, and the rumours die away.

A metà di una frase la voce della medium.easy: In the middle of a sentence the medium's voice changes: it gets lower and slower, with an accent you have only heard in family stories. It is Grandfather. He calls you by name and tells you that in the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper: one finger would be enough to make a hole in it. Then the candle goes out, and the voice is silent.
A metà di una frase la voce della medium.short: The medium's voice becomes Grandfather's: "In the fog the veil is as thin as wet paper. One finger could pierce it." Then the candle goes out.

L'Asylum Program è una vecchia caserma i.easy: The Asylum Program is an old barracks painted white, with bars on the windows and an iron cross on the gate. Father Anzelm, bent with age now, runs it with two nuns and a huge orderly who never speaks. The fog has brought the "possessed" here: people who speak with voices not their own, who write in languages they never learned, who knock on the walls for hours.
L'Asylum Program è una vecchia caserma i.short: At the Asylum Program, Father Anzelm treats the fog's "possessed": people who speak in others' voices and knock on the walls for hours.

La cura è severa: bagni gelati, preghier.easy: The cure is hard: freezing baths, prayers, leather straps, silence. In a way it does you good to see how small the difference is between them and you. But the man in cell number seven, when you walk past, stops knocking and says hello using your name, and your grandfather's voice.
La cura è severa: bagni gelati, preghier.short: The cure is harsh, and it does you good. But the man in cell seven greets you by name, in your grandfather's voice.

Per la notte di Ognissanti Madame Vámos.easy: For All Saints' night Madame Vámos invites the whole village to the Temple of the Circle, or to the part of it that has been built. Two hundred people come, with lanterns, through the fog. In the middle of the hall there is a round table, with a chair for each heir of the estate and two more chairs: one for Madame and one empty.
Per la notte di Ognissanti Madame Vámos.short: On All Saints' night two hundred people cross the fog to the Temple. At the table, a chair for each heir, one for Madame, and one empty.

Madame annuncia che stanotte, con l'aiut.easy: Madame says that tonight, with the help of the founder's blood, she will try to call him: the man who first wrote that veils can be lifted. {0} writes the record, because the medium wants it: "so it is written by a hand of the family".
Madame annuncia che stanotte, con l'aiut.short: Madame will try to summon the founder, with the help of his blood. {0} takes the minutes, "a hand of the family".

Senza una medium, la famiglia fa da sé..easy: There is no medium, so the family does it alone. On All Saints' night the heirs sit around the old table in the laboratory, the one Grandfather used for his experiments with magnetism. The Journal is open at the last page and there is an empty chair at the head of the table. {0} writes the record.
Senza una medium, la famiglia fa da sé..short: Without a medium, the heirs sit alone around the old laboratory table, an empty chair at its head. {0} takes the minutes.

Fuori la nebbia preme contro i vetri. Ne.easy: Outside, the fog presses against the windows. None of them has ever led a séance, but they have all read enough to know how to do it. That is exactly what is most frightening.
Fuori la nebbia preme contro i vetri. Ne.short: None of them has ever led a séance, but all of them know how. That is what is frightening.

A mezzanotte la fiamma della candela, al.easy: At midnight the candle flame, in the middle of the table, bends towards the empty chair, as if blown by a breath of air. It is time to decide.
A mezzanotte la fiamma della candela, al.short: At midnight the flame bends towards the empty chair. It is time to decide.

Madame Vámos chiude gli occhi e si irrig.easy: Madame Vámos closes her eyes and goes stiff in her chair. She opens her lips, and slowly a white, glowing substance begins to come out of her mouth, like heavy smoke. It stretches across the table towards the empty chair and takes the shape of a hand. Then an arm. Someone screams. The light becomes very bright.
Madame Vámos chiude gli occhi e si irrig.short: A white, glowing substance pours from Madame's mouth, stretches towards the empty chair and takes the shape of a hand. The light blinds everyone.

Quando torna il buio, sulla sedia di Mad.easy: When the dark comes back, there is only her black shawl on Madame's chair. Her body is gone. On the table there is a pool of white substance, still warm, and someone, with a shaking hand, puts it into a vial.
Quando torna il buio, sulla sedia di Mad.short: In the dark, only her shawl is left on Madame's chair. Someone gathers the white substance on the table into a vial.

Madame Vámos rovescia la testa all'indie.easy: Madame Vámos tips her head back. From her mouth comes a white, stringy substance that makes a small glowing pool on the table. The empty chair creaks, as if someone had just sat down. Then Madame coughs, wipes her lips with a handkerchief and says, in her normal voice: "He was here."
Madame Vámos rovescia la testa all'indie.short: A white, glowing substance flows from Madame's mouth; the empty chair creaks. Then Madame wipes her lips: "He was here."

Il medico, il giorno dopo, dirà che era.easy: The next day the doctor will say it was gauze soaked in phosphorus. But the substance someone put in a vial is still glowing, months later.
Il medico, il giorno dopo, dirà che era.short: Gauze and phosphorus, the doctor will say. But the vial still glows months later.

A mezzanotte la persona più giovane sedu.easy: At midnight the youngest person at the table starts to speak with a voice that is not their own: low, slow, impatient. It says three words in an ancient language, then coughs, and a white, stringy substance that glows in the dark comes out of their mouth.
A mezzanotte la persona più giovane sedu.short: At midnight the youngest speaks in a voice not their own, then coughs up a white substance that glows in the dark.

Al mattino nessuno ricorda chi abbia pre.easy: In the morning no one remembers who took a vial from the laboratory to collect it. But the vial is full.
Al mattino nessuno ricorda chi abbia pre.short: No one remembers who gathered it. But the vial is full.

Qualcuno si alza di scatto e spalanca le.easy: Someone suddenly stands up and opens the shutters. The candle goes out. The empty chair falls over by itself, with a thud. For a long moment no one breathes.
Qualcuno si alza di scatto e spalanca le.short: Someone throws open the shutters. The candle goes out and the empty chair falls by itself.

Poi, fuori, la nebbia si dirada un poco,.easy: Then, outside, the fog gets a little thinner, and for the first time in months you can see the moon. Whatever was waiting on the other side of the table has gone. But it has gone away angry, and all winter, at the estate, the doors slam by themselves.
Poi, fuori, la nebbia si dirada un poco,.short: The fog thins and the moon returns. Whatever was waiting has gone, but angry: all winter the doors slam by themselves.

Qualche settimana dopo la seduta, Madame.easy: A few weeks after the séance, Madame Vámos sends each heir a card with a black border. She writes that she does not have much time left, or perhaps she has too much. Anyway, the moment has come to leave someone her most precious secret: the way not to die completely.
Qualche settimana dopo la seduta, Madame.short: Madame Vámos writes to the heirs: it is time to leave someone her most precious secret, the way not to die entirely.

Lo venderà a una persona soltanto: a chi.easy: She will sell it to only one person: whoever shows they want it most. "My spiritual children," she writes at the end of the card, "will understand that even eternity costs something."
Lo venderà a una persona soltanto: a chi.short: She will sell it to whoever wants it most: "even eternity has a price".

Il Sindaco Bódi, figlio di quello che se.easy: Mayor Bódi, son of the man who was on the council in 1856, is ill and is looking for someone to take his place in politics.

Con l'ultimo filo saldato, il secondo st.easy: When the last wire is soldered, the second part of the Telegraph switches on. The glass jars give a milk-white light, the bone keyboard vibrates and the needle no longer shakes: it moves surely from key to key and, for the first time, writes a whole word.
Con l'ultimo filo saldato, il secondo st.short: With the last wire soldered, the Telegraph comes alive, and for the first time the needle spells a whole word.

È un nome. Nessuno in famiglia lo conosc.easy: It is a name. No one in the family knows it. But the next morning, at the cemetery, they find it written on a headstone the gravedigger swears he has never seen.
È un nome. Nessuno in famiglia lo conosc.short: It is an unknown name. The next day they find it on a headstone no one had ever seen.

Pezzo dopo pezzo, senza aspettare il con.easy: Piece by piece, without waiting for anyone's permission, the first part of the Telegraph is finally built against the laboratory wall. When you switch it on, the lights in the whole house get dimmer and the needle, inside the flask, starts to shake. It is looking for a letter. It cannot find it yet.
Pezzo dopo pezzo, senza aspettare il con.short: On your own, you build the Telegraph's first stage. When you switch it on the needle trembles, seeking a letter it cannot yet find.

Saldi un altro tratto di filo, tari l'ag.easy: You solder another piece of wire, adjust the needle, replace a broken jar. The machine grows, but the needle does not move: some pieces are still missing. As you put the tools away, you think you hear an impatient knock inside the flask.
Saldi un altro tratto di filo, tari l'ag.short: The machine grows, but the needle stays still. As you put the tools away, an impatient knock comes from the flask.

**IL SINDACO E LE SUE AMICIZIE.** Il Sin.easy: **THE MAYOR AND HIS FRIENDS.** Mayor Bódi got his job from his father, the way other people inherit a watch. He has been ill for a long time and does not hide it. He also does not hide that he is looking, among the important families of {0}, for someone to protect in the coming years, who will protect him in return.
**IL SINDACO E LE SUE AMICIZIE.** Il Sin.short: **THE MAYOR AND HIS FRIENDSHIPS.** Mayor Bódi, ill, is looking among the families of {0} for someone to protect, and be protected by.

Corre voce che le famiglie della tenuta.easy: People say the families of the estate have already made their offers, with money and favours. This newspaper cannot confirm it, and its editor has been asked not to ask questions.
Corre voce che le famiglie della tenuta.short: They say the estate's families have already made their offers. The newspaper cannot confirm it.

Gli anni della vecchiaia passano in fret.easy: The late years go by quickly, as always for people with too many things to do. The fog rises and falls with the seasons, but it never goes away completely: it hides in the ditches, in the cemetery, behind the estate's greenhouses, and waits.
Gli anni della vecchiaia passano in fret.short: The late years pass quickly. The fog never quite leaves: it withdraws into the ditches and the cemetery, and waits.

Anche le carte della seconda generazione.easy: The papers of the second generation also end with a series of funerals. I wanted to check the headstones myself, one by one, with a lantern, because in the fog of the cemetery (yes, it is still there) nothing could be read. The dates are the same as in the records. But under each date, in smaller letters, the hour is carved too. And all those hours are between midnight and three.
Anche le carte della seconda generazione.short: The second generation also ends in the cemetery, in the fog. Under each date on the headstones an hour is carved: always between midnight and three.

Il lapicida, interrogato da un mio colle.easy: The stonemason, questioned by a colleague of mine in 1902, said he had never carved any hour.

Il telegramma raggiunse i nuovi eredi in.easy: The telegram reached the new heirs in faraway cities, in offices, laboratories, schools. When they got off the train (now the train went there too) they found a small town very different from the village of the family stories. There were street lamps along the main road, a telegraph office, a bank with fake marble columns and, in the café on the square, a phonograph that played Viennese waltzes for anyone who put in a coin.
Il telegramma raggiunse i nuovi eredi in.short: The telegram reached the new heirs far away. Off the train, they found a modern little town: street lamps, a telegraph, a bank and a phonograph playing waltzes.

E c'era il Circolo. Il Circolo dell'Ulti.easy: And there was the Circle. The Circle of the Last Hour no longer had to hide, and did not need to make itself known: it owned the undertaker's, half the buildings on the square and most of the town council. Its members wore a small silver eye on their jackets, and were proud to wear it.
E c'era il Circolo. Il Circolo dell'Ulti.short: The Circle now owned the undertaker's, half the square and the town council. Its members proudly wore a silver eye.

E c'era la Chiesa. Dopo anni di prediche.easy: And there was the Church. After years of sermons, trials and excommunications, the bishop had got what he wanted: the Circle of the Last Hour was banned, its séances were a crime, and anyone who spoke to the dead ended up before the Church court. Father Benedek, who had taken Father Anzelm's place, kept a list of names. The family's name was on it several times.
E c'era la Chiesa. Dopo anni di prediche.short: The Church had won: the Circle was outlawed and séances a crime. Father Benedek kept a register of names, and the family's appeared more than once.

E c'era, ancora, la vecchia guerra. Il C.easy: And the old war was still going on. The Circle of the Last Hour and the parish of Father Benedek, who had taken Father Anzelm's place, fought over the souls of {0} one at a time, like two neighbours quarrelling over the wall between their land. In this case, the wall was the veil.
E c'era, ancora, la vecchia guerra. Il C.short: The Circle and Father Benedek's parish still fought over the souls of {0}, like neighbours over a boundary wall. The wall was the veil.

Madame Vámos, a sentire la gente, aveva.easy: People said that Madame Vámos was the same age as fifty years before. No one knew where she lived. Everyone knew where to find her.

Di Madame Vámos restavano uno scialle ne.easy: Of Madame Vámos there was only a black shawl, kept in a glass case in the Temple of the Circle, and an empty chair that no one dared to move.

Ora i morti della famiglia sono due gene.easy: Now the family's dead are two generations. On the first night at the estate the knocking starts again, regular as a clock, but faster: two different rhythms that mix, interrupt and correct each other.
Ora i morti della famiglia sono due gene.short: On the first night the knocking returns, but now there are two rhythms, correcting each other.

Quando arrivano le voci, ogni erede ne s.easy: When the voices come, each heir hears two: their parent's, and an older, weaker one that they know only from portraits. They do not always agree.
Quando arrivano le voci, ogni erede ne s.short: Each heir hears two voices: a parent and an older ancestor. They do not always agree.

Le due voci parlano insieme, una sopra l.easy: The two voices talk together, one over the other, about the same thing: a formula, an obsession, an idea that has used up two lives and now looks for a third. When one stops to breathe, the other finishes the sentence.
Le due voci parlano insieme, una sopra l.short: Two voices, one obsession, which consumed two lives and now seeks a third.

Non litigano. Sono d'accordo su tutto, e.easy: They do not argue. They agree about everything, and that is what scares you. At dawn you notice you are finishing their sentences out loud.
Non litigano. Sono d'accordo su tutto, e.short: They agree on everything. At dawn you are finishing their sentences aloud.

\"È di famiglia\", dice la voce più anti.easy: "It runs in the family," says the older voice, almost proudly. "It runs in the family," your parent's voice repeats, almost as if saying sorry.

Poi entrambe ti spiegano, per tutta la n.easy: Then both of them explain to you, all night, an idea that will never leave you. In the morning you do not remember the words. You only remember that you must do something, and that you must do it soon.
Poi entrambe ti spiegano, per tutta la n.short: All night they explain an idea to you. In the morning you only know you must act, and soon.

La voce del tuo genitore è febbrile: par.easy: Your parent's voice is agitated: it speaks fast, says one thing and then the opposite, starts again, asks you to finish a job without saying which. Then, softly, the other, older voice speaks: "Calm. Let the living breathe."
La voce del tuo genitore è febbrile: par.short: Your parent's voice is feverish and confused. The other, older one calms it: "Let the living breathe."

Per un poco la voce febbrile tace. Ma pr.easy: For a while the agitated voice is quiet. But before dawn it comes back, alone, and whispers one last thing in your ear.

Colpi rapidi, nervosi, come di dita che.easy: Fast, nervous knocking, like fingers that cannot stay still. It is the voice you know best, but you have never heard it like this: anxious, hungry, full of numbers. The older voice tries to cover it with an old family lullaby, out of tune and patient.
Colpi rapidi, nervosi, come di dita che.short: The voice you know best is anxious and full of numbers. The older one tries to soothe it with a lullaby.

Ti addormenti a metà della ninna nanna..easy: You fall asleep in the middle of the lullaby. When you wake up, there is an idea in your head that is not yours.

Le due voci arrivano insieme, e sono ser.easy: The two voices come together, and they are calm. They tell you about a crowd on the other side: the families your family has helped in fifty years of grief. Now they are all in line to say thank you. "They will not leave you without protection," says the older voice.
Le due voci arrivano insieme, e sono ser.short: On the other side, the families comforted over fifty years have lined up to give thanks. "They will protect you," says the older voice.

Al mattino, per la prima volta da quando.easy: In the morning, for the first time since you came here, the neighbours' dogs are happy to see you. And in the letterbox there is an unsigned envelope with money inside.
Al mattino, per la prima volta da quando.short: In the morning the dogs greet you happily, and there is an envelope of money in the letterbox.

Nessun colpo: un fruscio, come di tante.easy: No knocking: only a rustle, like many people quietly coming into a room. Your ancestors' voices introduce you, one at a time, to dozens of strangers: the miller's widow, a child who died of fever, a miner, a dressmaker. Each one shakes your hand, cold and light. "We owe you a favour," they say.
Nessun colpo: un fruscio, come di tante.short: A rustle of footsteps: your ancestors introduce you to dozens of dead the family once comforted. "We owe you a favour."

Il giorno dopo, in paese, la gente ti sa.easy: The next day, in town, people say hello to you in the street, and the grocer does not want your money.

La voce del tuo genitore è bassa, come d.easy: Your parent's voice is low, like someone afraid of being heard. "The promise to the Circle. You don't know it, but I do: the one who came before me told me, and now it's your turn to carry it."
La voce del tuo genitore è bassa, come d.short: "The promise to the Circle. The one before me revealed it to me. Now it's your turn."

Poi la voce più antica, fioca, aggiunge.easy: Then the older voice, weak, tells you the rest: how to break the promise, and how to make the one who wanted it pay dearly. It makes you write everything on the back of a family photograph.
Poi la voce più antica, fioca, aggiunge.short: The older voice tells you how to break the promise, and make it cost dearly. You write it all on the back of a photograph.

\"Il Circolo busserà\", dice la voce più.easy: "The Circle will knock," says the older voice. "It will knock at your door, because I was the one who signed." "And you will not open," says the other, "or you will open on our terms."
\"Il Circolo busserà\", dice la voce più.short: "The Circle will knock for you." "And you will not open, or you will open on our terms."

Per tutta la notte le due voci ti insegn.easy: All night the two voices teach you the exact words, the dates, the names: enough to break the promise, or to blackmail the people who keep it. In the morning you have a folder of notes and you know very well what it is worth.
Per tutta la notte le due voci ti insegn.short: All night you learn words, dates and names: enough to break the promise, or blackmail those who keep it.

Le voci sono deboli, lontane, come su un.easy: The voices are weak and far away, like on a bad telegraph line. You hear your name, then a word that may be "careful" or may be "patience", and then nothing more.
Le voci sono deboli, lontane, come su un.short: Faint, crackling voices: your name, an unclear word, then nothing.

Aspetti a lungo. Alla fine arrivano due.easy: You wait a long time. In the end two very soft knocks come, one for each of the voices you hoped to hear. Then a rustle of paper, as if someone were turning the pages of a book on the other side of the wall.
Aspetti a lungo. Alla fine arrivano due.short: After a long wait, two faint knocks and a rustle of pages behind the wall.

La mattina dopo, prima ancora di colazio.easy: The next morning, even before breakfast, someone knocks at the front door. Luckily, they knock in a normal way. It is an old man with a white beard and a doctor's bag. He says he is Dr Lukács, professor at the University and, in his own words, "the last reasonable man in {0}".
La mattina dopo, prima ancora di colazio.short: In the morning Dr Lukács of the University knocks, normally, thank goodness: "the last reasonable man in {0}".

Lukács ha settant'anni, una memoria ecce.easy: Lukács is seventy, has an excellent memory and only one obsession: to prove that no one in {0} has ever spoken to the dead. "I went to the Circle's séances for twenty years and took notes," he says. "I have seen tables fly and ghosts made of gauze and phosphorus. I have collected evidence. I only need someone from the family who wants to help me."
Lukács ha settant'anni, una memoria ecce.short: Lukács wants to prove that no one in {0} ever spoke with the dead. He has twenty years of notes and evidence: he needs someone from the family.

In piazza aprono negozi nuovi, tutti nel.easy: New shops open on the square, all in the same month and all paid for in cash.

Nel suo studio all'University il dottor.easy: In his study at the University Dr Lukács has made a small museum of tricks. There are very thin black silk threads for lifting a table; a pair of shoes with hollow heels, for knocking on the floor without using your hands; a gauze mask still dirty with phosphorus; and many receipts from a blacksmith, in the name of the Circle of the Last Hour, for "work on the walls" in private houses.
Nel suo studio all'University il dottor.short: Lukács has a small museum of fraud: silk threads to lift tables, shoes for knocking, a phosphorus mask and receipts from a smith the Circle paid for "work on the walls".

Lo aiuti a catalogare tutto, a confronta.easy: You help him put everything in order, compare the dates, work out who knew what. It is long, careful work, and it calms you. When you leave, the world seems simpler.
Lo aiuti a catalogare tutto, a confronta.short: You help him sort the evidence. When you leave, the world seems simpler.

Le pompe funebri del Circolo sono le più.easy: The Circle's undertaker's is the most elegant in the region: black marble, purple velvet, an organ that plays by itself. Here the dead are washed, perfumed, dressed in white and buried with a silver bell on the wrist. A cord connects it to another bell above the grave. "So they can ring," the director explains with a professional smile. "If they ever want to."
Le pompe funebri del Circolo sono le più.short: At the Circle's undertaker's the dead are buried with a bell on the wrist, joined to one above the grave. "Should they ever wish to ring," the director smiles.

Nel retrobottega ti mostra il registro d.easy: In the back room he shows you the burial book. Next to several names, in pencil, there is a small cross and a date after the funeral: the days when the bell rang. Then he offers you, at a good price, something for your laboratory. You do not ask which coffin it came from.
Nel retrobottega ti mostra il registro d.short: In the register, beside some names, is the date the bell rang. Then he sells you something for the laboratory. You do not ask where it came from.

**NEGOZI NUOVI, CLIENTI POCHI.** Nell'ul.easy: **NEW SHOPS, FEW CUSTOMERS.** In the last month some new shops have opened in {0}, one after another, all with freshly painted signs and perfect windows. According to the land office, a Budapest company paid for them in cash, but no one knows who its partners are. None of the shops seems to have many customers, but they all stay open late.
**NEGOZI NUOVI, CLIENTI POCHI.** Nell'ul.short: **NEW SHOPS, FEW CUSTOMERS.** New shops in {0}, paid in cash by a mysterious Budapest company. Few customers, yet they stay open late.

Il dottor Lukács, interpellato da questo.easy: Dr Lukács, interviewed by this newspaper, is sure: these shops are a cover for the Circle of the Last Hour, which carries on its activities behind them in secret. The Circle replied with a black-bordered card: "Trade is also a way to console."
Il dottor Lukács, interpellato da questo.short: Lukács says they are fronts for the Circle. The Circle replies: "Trade, too, is a form of consolation."

Saldi l'ultimo filo con le mani che trem.easy: You solder the last wire with shaking hands. Before you can turn the switch, the Telegraph turns on by itself. The glass jars light up one after another, like the windows of a house at sunset, and a low hum fills the laboratory, the estate, maybe the whole town.
Saldi l'ultimo filo con le mani che trem.short: At the last wire the Telegraph switches itself on, and a hum fills the estate, perhaps the town.

L'ago si alza, esita, poi comincia a bat.easy: The needle rises, waits a moment, then begins to tap on the bone keys, slowly and surely. It writes a name: your family's. Then it stops and waits, like someone who has rung a doorbell.
L'ago si alza, esita, poi comincia a bat.short: The needle taps out your family's name, then waits, like someone who has rung a doorbell.

**LO SCANDALO DEL CIRCOLO.** La Gazzetta.easy: **THE SCANDAL OF THE CIRCLE.** The Gazette publishes on its front page, across six columns, the evidence found by Dr Lukács: the blacksmith's receipts, the exposed shops, the confessions of two former members. In a week almost everyone leaves the Circle of the Last Hour, and on the square someone throws stones at its windows.
**LO SCANDALO DEL CIRCOLO.** La Gazzetta.short: **THE SCANDAL OF THE CIRCLE.** The Gazette prints Lukács's evidence. Within a week the Circle loses its members, and stones fly on the square.

Madame Vámos, convocata dal pretore, non.easy: Madame Vámos is called by the judge, but she does not come. Some say she has packed her bags. Others say she has no bags to pack.

Nessuno ha toccato le facciate. Le botte.easy: No one has touched the fake shops. The Circle's shops stay open late, with perfect windows and few customers. Dr Lukács writes angry letters to the Gazette, but the Gazette does not print them.
Nessuno ha toccato le facciate. Le botte.short: No one has touched the fronts, and the Gazette does not print Lukács's furious letters.

Il Circolo, in silenzio, ringrazia: una.easy: The Circle, without a word, says thank you: one morning each heir finds a fresh black carnation in front of the door.

Una facciata è caduta, e quello che c'er.easy: One fake shop has been exposed, and in a day the whole town knows what it was hiding. But the others are still open, and the Circle denies everything with great dignity.
Una facciata è caduta, e quello che c'er.short: One front has fallen, but the others hold, and the Circle denies everything.

{0} non sa più a chi credere. La gente v.easy: In {0} no one knows whom to believe any more. To be safe, people go to mass on Sunday and to séances on Thursday.

Alla fine di questa Generazione, tutta l.easy: At the end of this Generation, the whole town will sit at the same table.

L'ultima notte del 1905 {0} si riunisce.easy: On the last night of 1905 all of {0} meets in the great hall of the town hall: the mayor, the council, the Circle, the parish, Dr Lukács with his notebook and, in the middle, the family of the estate. Two hundred people sit in circles, each holding their neighbours' hands, and the lights are off. No one remembers who called them. But everyone has come.
L'ultima notte del 1905 {0} si riunisce.short: On the last night of 1905 two hundred people sit in circles in the town hall of {0}, hand in hand, in the dark. No one knows who summoned them, but all have come.

A mezzanotte meno un quarto i colpi comi.easy: At a quarter to twelve the knocking begins. Not on the walls: everywhere. In the floor, in the ceiling, in the chairs, in everyone's chest. Fifty-seven years after that first night, the veil has never been so thin.
A mezzanotte meno un quarto i colpi comi.short: At a quarter to midnight the knocking starts everywhere, even in their chests. The veil has never been so thin.

Qualcuno ha portato il Telegrafo dalla t.easy: Someone has brought the Telegraph from the estate on a cart and connected it to the town hall's electric wires. The needle taps by itself, impatient, waiting for instructions.
Qualcuno ha portato il Telegrafo dalla t.short: The Telegraph, wired to the town hall's lights, taps by itself, impatient.

Nell'aria, al centro della sala, si apre.easy: In the air, in the middle of the hall, a thin crack opens, like in glass. On the other side there is a cold light, and something moving.

Il velo trema, ma tiene. Quando le lampa.easy: The veil shakes, but it holds. When the lights come back on, everyone looks at the Circle's table.

Egregio dottore, mi chiede che cosa acca.easy: Dear Doctor, you ask me what happened on the night of 31 December 1905. I will tell you, even if you will not believe me. And even though you only need to leave the sacristy and walk a little on the square to see it with your own eyes.
Egregio dottore, mi chiede che cosa acca.short: Dear Doctor, you ask about the night of 31 December 1905. You will not believe me, but you need only step into the square to see.

Votammo di aprire. Il Telegrafo, o la me.easy: We voted to open. The Telegraph, or the medium, or our joined hands (I no longer know what the key was) turned in the lock, and the veil tore like an old curtain. There was no flash and no thunder. Only a great cold. Then the door of the hall opened by itself, and people came in. People we knew. People we had buried.
Votammo di aprire. Il Telegrafo, o la me.short: We voted to open, and the veil tore like an old curtain. In a great cold, people we had buried came in through the door.

Sono rimasti. A {0} i morti camminano co.easy: They stayed. In {0} the dead walk with the living, eat at their tables, vote in the council, complain about the price of bread. At first it was easy to recognise them: they were paler, quieter, and had no shadow. Now it is not so easy.
Sono rimasti. A {0} i morti camminano co.short: They stayed. In {0} the dead live among the living. At first you could tell them apart. Not any more.

Lei mi chiede da quale parte del velo le.easy: You ask me which side of the veil I am writing from. Honestly, Doctor, I stopped asking myself some years ago.

Egregio dottore, il Telegrafo era finito.easy: Dear Doctor, the Telegraph was finished. You only had to turn a dial to hear Father's voice, and turn it the other way to close the door for ever. We voted to close it.
Egregio dottore, il Telegrafo era finito.short: Dear Doctor, with the Telegraph we could hear Father or close the door for ever. We voted to close it.

La macchina urlò per un'ora, poi tacque..easy: The machine screamed for an hour, then stopped. Since that night no séance has ever worked again: not in {0}, not in Vienna, not in London. Tables stay on the floor, mediums work in the theatre, and your Society studies nothing very seriously. I am sorry.
La macchina urlò per un'ora, poi tacque..short: The machine screamed, then fell silent. Since then no séance has worked anywhere. My apologies to your Society.

Anche la voce del padre è rimasta dall'a.easy: Father's voice also stayed on the other side. We will never know what he wanted to tell us. Sometimes, at night, I put my hand on the wall of my room, the one where they used to knock, and wait. The wall is cold and silent, and I sleep very well.
Anche la voce del padre è rimasta dall'a.short: We will never know what Father wanted to tell us. Sometimes at night I touch the wall where they used to knock. It is silent, and I sleep very well.

Egregio dottore, era tutto un trucco. Il.easy: Dear Doctor, it was all a trick. Dr Lukács had always said so, and in the end we proved it in front of all {0}. There were black silk threads to lift the table, a blacksmith working with them for the knocking in the walls, gauze and phosphorus for the ectoplasm, and many spies (widows, innkeepers, the sexton) who told the Circle everyone's secrets. The voices of the dead were the voices of the living, well paid.
Egregio dottore, era tutto un trucco. Il.short: Dear Doctor, it was all a trick: silk threads, a smith in on it, gauze and phosphorus, a network of informers. The voices of the dead were the living, well paid.

La nostra famiglia divenne celebre. Scri.easy: Our family became famous. We wrote books, gave talks in Budapest and Paris and exposed thirty-two cheating mediums in eleven countries. Your Society even gave us a medal, which I keep in a drawer.
La nostra famiglia divenne celebre. Scri.short: We became famous: books, lectures, thirty-two mediums exposed. And a medal, in a drawer.

Le scrivo però per dirle una cosa che no.easy: But I am writing to tell you something I have never said in public. The blacksmith, when questioned, admitted he had knocked on the walls of the estate for twenty years, because the Circle asked him to. But the knocking on the first night, 2 November 1848, was not his: he was six years old then.
Le scrivo però per dirle una cosa che no.short: But the smith, who knocked for the Circle for twenty years, was six years old on the first night, in 1848.

E certe notti, ancora oggi, alla tenuta.easy: And some nights, even today, someone knocks at the estate. One knock, then two, then one.

Egregio dottore, il Telegrafo batté per.easy: Dear Doctor, the Telegraph tapped for three days and three nights. The needle ran over the bone keys faster than we could write, and we took turns at the table every two hours, with fingers black with ink. It was him, without doubt: the same abbreviations, the same mistakes, the same impatience as in the Journal.
Egregio dottore, il Telegrafo batté per.short: Dear Doctor, the Telegraph tapped for three days and nights, and we transcribed in shifts. It was him: the same mistakes, the same impatience as the Journal.

Non ci chiese come stavamo. Non ci disse.easy: He did not ask how we were. He did not tell us what it was like on the other side.
